description: Born in Rome to Marcus Antonius Creticus and Julia Antonia. Birth year disputed between 86 and 83 BCE.

event_title: Cavalry command in Syria and Egypt
description: Served as praefectus equitum under Aulus Gabinius, proconsul of Syria. Participated in campaigns against Aristobulus II in Judaea and the restoration of Ptolemy XII Auletes in Egypt.
Joined Caesar in Gaul as a military officer. Gained combat experience and Caesar's trust during the late Gallic campaigns.
Elected tribune for 49 BCE. Entered office and became Caesar's key political agent in Rome during the escalating crisis.

Antony's tribunician veto was overridden by the senatus consultum ultimum. He fled Rome in disguise with Quintus Cassius Longinus to join Caesar at Ravenna. Caesar used this as justification for crossing the Rubicon.
Commanded the left wing of Caesar's army against Pompey's forces at Pharsalus. Caesar's decisive victory.
Caesar appointed Antony Master of Horse, making him the ranking official in Italy while Caesar pursued Pompey to Egypt and fought the Alexandrine War.
During the Lupercalia festival, Antony publicly offered a royal diadem to Caesar three times. Caesar refused each time to applause from the crowd.
Caesar was assassinated in the Senate. Antony was detained outside by Trebonius and escaped. He initially negotiated an amnesty with the conspirators.
Antony delivered the funeral oration for Caesar, reading his will and displaying the blood-stained toga, which incited the crowd against the assassins.
Antony besieged Decimus Brutus at Mutina. Defeated by Octavian and the consuls Hirtius and Pansa (both killed). Antony retreated across the Alps to Gaul.
Antony, Octavian, and Lepidus met near Bononia and formed the Second Triumvirate, ratified by the Lex Titia on 27 November 43 BCE. The triumvirs divided the Roman world and initiated proscriptions.
Cicero was captured and killed at Caieta. His head and hands were displayed on the Rostra in Rome on Antony's orders.
Two engagements at Philippi in Macedonia. Antony defeated Cassius (first battle) and combined with Octavian to defeat Brutus (second battle). Cassius and Brutus both committed suicide.
Antony summoned Cleopatra VII to Tarsus in Cilicia to answer for her alleged support of Cassius. She arrived in spectacular fashion; Antony was captivated and accompanied her to Alexandria.
Antony spent the winter of 41–40 BCE in Alexandria with Cleopatra. Their twins Alexander Helios and Cleopatra Selene were born in 40 BCE.

Antony and Octavian reconciled at Brundisium after the Perusine War. They formally divided the Roman world: Antony took the East, Octavian the West, Lepidus Africa. Antony married Octavia to seal the pact.

Antony invaded Parthian territory with c. 100,000 troops. The campaign was a disaster: his siege train was captured, and he lost c. 20,000 infantry and 4,000 cavalry during a winter retreat through Armenia.
Antony captured the Armenian king Artavasdes II and annexed Armenia. He celebrated a quasi-triumph in Alexandria rather than Rome.

Antony staged a grand ceremony in the Gymnasium of Alexandria, proclaiming Cleopatra 'Queen of Kings' and assigning Roman eastern territories to her children. Octavian used this as propaganda against Antony.

event_title: Divorce of Octavia and declaration of war
description: Antony formally divorced Octavia. Octavian obtained Antony's will from the Vestal Virgins and read it to the Senate. The Senate stripped Antony of his powers and declared war on Cleopatra VII.
Naval battle off the coast of Actium, Greece. Octavian's fleet under Agrippa defeated Antony and Cleopatra's combined fleet. Cleopatra's squadron withdrew; Antony followed, abandoning his fleet.

After Octavian's forces entered Alexandria and Antony's remaining troops defected, Antony stabbed himself with his sword. He was carried to Cleopatra's mausoleum and died in her arms. Cleopatra followed in suicide on 10 August.
